summary: U.S. veterans and Japanese officials marked the 70th anniversary of the Battle of Iwo Jima on the island’s beaches and Mount Suribachi. Veterans reflected on the fierce fighting and shared mixed feelings toward former enemies, while Japanese leaders emphasized the shared sacrifice that built present peace. The ceremony highlighted the battle’s enduring legacy, with memorials and the attendance of the last surviving Medal of Honor recipient, Woody Williams.
reference:
More than 30 veterans flew to the island of Iwo Jima, Japan, on Saturday .
The 1945 battle was one of the bloodiest of World War 11 .
Represents a major invasion and win for the U.S.
The Battle of Iwojima lasted about a month .
About 22,000 Japanese soldiers and 7,000 U.S. servicemen died .

summary:
Five sealed bottles of grey “wine” were recovered from the 1864 Civil War blockade‑runner Mary‑Celestia in a secret locker.  
At a Charleston festival, a panel of sommeliers uncorked the wine and described it as sulphur‑heavy, crab‑water, gasoline‑tinged, and largely unpalatable.  
Chemical testing revealed 37 % alcohol and a mix of camphor, hydrocarbons, turpentine and sulphur compounds.
reference:
Bottle of grey liquid was recovered from a US Civil War shipwreck .
Mary-Celestia steamship sank under mysterious circumstances in 1864 .
Wine bottle was uncorked at a food festival in Charleston, South Carolina .
Sommeliers who sipped the liquid inside said it smelled and tasted like a mix of crab water, gasoline, salt water and vinegar, with hints of citrus .

summary:
Bernard Jordan, a 19‑year‑old Royal Navy lieutenant, famously escaped from a care home to attend the 75th‑anniversary D‑Day commemorations in Normandy and later had his medals sold for £1,650—over five times the £300 estimate—benefiting the RNLI.  
After his death in 2024 and the subsequent passing of his widow, their estate left £600,000 to the RNLI.  
Jordan’s medals included the 1939‑1945 Star, Atlantic Star with French and German clasp, Italy Star, Defence Medal and War Medal, and he had also served as a long‑time councillor and mayor of Hove.
reference:
Bernard Jordan went missing from his care home before D-Day anniversary .
He caught a ferry to Caen, Normandy and made his own way to the service .
He died aged 90 on December 30, and a week later his widow passed away .
Mr Jordan's medals have sold for £1,650 - the estimate had been just £300 .
Money raised donated to RNLI, together with £600,000 left in couple's will .

summary: Queensland grandmother charged with attempted murder of two step‑grandchildren and other child‑related offences has been released on bail and moved into an apartment opposite two schools. She allegedly set a bedroom on fire and blocked the boys’ escape route, and police also suspect her in earlier child deaths. The court granted bail with a condition she have no contact with anyone under 18 and did not view her as a particular risk despite the schools’ proximity.
reference:
Queensland grandmother, 58,  who was charged with four counts of attempted child murder, has been released from prison on bail .
The grandmother is accused of trying to kill two of her step grandchildren by setting their bedroom on fire.
She is also accused of killing two other children from the same family in the Morayfield 'house of horrors' between 2013 and 2014 .
Parents are angry to find the woman has moved to a unit across the road from two Queensland schools .
The grandmother has said she is 'not a heartless person' and claimed 'only a person with no heart' would commit such crimes .
